     1→# PostHog Analytics Integration for SpecStory CLI
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→This workplan outlines the integration of PostHog analytics into the SpecStory CLI using the official PostHog Go library. The integration will track key usage events to help understand user behavior and improve the product.
     6→
     7→## Events to Track
     8→
     9→| Event Name            | Event Key                   | Description                                                  | Status        |
    10→|-----------------------|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
    11→| Extension Activated   | `ext_activated`             | Triggered when extension is loaded in interactive mode       | ✅ Implemented |
    12→| Autosave Success      | `ext_autosave_success`      | Triggered when a new session is autosaved for the first time | ✅ Implemented |
    13→| Autosave Error        | `ext_autosave_error`        | Triggered when autosave fails for a new session              | ✅ Implemented |
    14→| Sync Markdown Success | `ext_sync_markdown_success` | Triggered when --sync-markdown command runs successfully     | ✅ Implemented |
    15→| Sync Markdown Error   | `ext_sync_markdown_error`   | Triggered when --sync-markdown command fails                 | ✅ Implemented |
    16→
    17→## Common Properties
    18→  - `cli_command` - Full command line used ✅
    19→  - `$device_id` - Shared analytics ID ✅
    20→  - `project_path` - Current working directory ✅
    21→  - `editor_name` - Always "Claude Code" for this CLI ✅
    22→  - `editor_type` - Always "claude code" for this CLI ✅
    23→  - `extension_version` - Version of this CLI (same as `specstory --version`) ✅
    24→  - `os_arch` - System architecture (e.g. arm64) ✅
    25→  - `os_name` - Operating system name (e.g. Darwin) ✅
    26→  - `os_platform` - Operating system platform (e.g. darwin) ✅
    27→  - `os_version` - Operating system version (e.g. 24.5.0) ✅
    28→  - `claude_code_version` - Version of Claude Code being used ❌
    29→    - Not implemented because it would require a claude version check which would create a delay for the user
    30→
    31→## Implementation Status
    32→
    33→### Completed Features
    34→- ✅ PostHog Go library integrated
    35→- ✅ Analytics package created with event tracking
    36→- ✅ Shared analytics ID implementation (macOS only)
    37→- ✅ Automatic inclusion of common properties:
    38→  - `cli_command` - Full command line used
    39→  - `$device_id` - Shared analytics ID
    40→  - `project_path` - Current working directory
    41→- ✅ GeoIP enabled for client-side tracking
    42→- ✅ Event tracking implemented:
    43→  - `ext_activated` - Tracks when Claude Code is launched
    44→  - `ext_autosave_success` - Tracks first-time autosave of new sessions
    45→  - `ext_autosave_error` - Tracks when first-time autosave fails
    46→  - `ext_sync_markdown_success` - Tracks successful markdown sync with session count
    47→  - `ext_sync_markdown_error` - Tracks sync failures with error details
    48→- ✅ `--no-usage-analytics` flag for opting out
    49→
    50→## Requirements
    51→- Create a --no-usage-analytics flag that allows the user to run without any analytics tracking ✅
    52→- If specstory cli is installed as part of BearClaude UI, align tracking identifiers for the two so events coming from the CLI and events coming from the UI have the same analytics identifier ✅
    53→
    54→## Shared Analytics ID Implementation
    55→
    56→### Overview
    57→To align analytics identifiers between BearClaude UI and specstory CLI, both applications will share a common analytics ID stored in a JSON file. This shared ID approach is only used on macOS where BearClaude runs. On other platforms, specstory CLI falls back to generating its own ID.
    58→
    59→### Shared File Location (macOS only)
    60→```
    61→~/Library/Application Support/SpecStory/analytics-id.json
    62→```
    63→
    64→### JSON File Format
    65→```json
    66→{
    67→  "analytics_id": "uuid-here",
    68→  "created_at": "2025-01-20T10:00:00Z",
    69→  "source": "specstory-cli"  // or "BearClaude"
    70→}
    71→```
    72→
    73→### Implementation Strategy
    74→1. Check if running on macOS (runtime.GOOS == "darwin")
    75→2. If on macOS:
    76→   - Check if the shared analytics file exists
    77→   - If exists, read and use the existing analytics_id
    78→   - If not exists:
    79→     - Create the directory structure if needed
    80→     - Generate a new UUID for analytics_id
    81→     - Write the JSON file with metadata
    82→3. If not on macOS or if shared ID fails:
    83→   - Fall back to hostname/username hash (original behavior)
    84→4. Use the determined ID as the PostHog distinct ID
    85→
    86→### Benefits
    87→- Single user identity across both tools
    88→- Standard macOS location for application data
    89→- No special permissions required
    90→- Clean separation with vendor-specific directory
    91→## Implementation Plan
    92→
    93→### Make analytics fairly self contained
    94→Create separation for the analytics functionality in the go app
    95→
    96→### Configuration
    97→
    98→The PostHog API key is injected at build time via ldflags in production builds. See `.goreleaser.yml` for the build configuration and `.github/workflows/release.yml` for how the `POSTHOG_API_KEY` secret is passed to GoReleaser.
    99→
   100→Development builds have analytics disabled by default (empty API key).
   101→

   103→
   104→Update README.md with:
   105→- Information about analytics collection
   106→- How to opt-out
   107→- What data is collected
   108→- Privacy policy
   109→

    19→	EventAutosaveError          = "ext_autosave_error"           // Tracks when an error occurs generating or writing markdown during `run`
    20→	EventSyncMarkdownNew        = "ext_sync_markdown_new"        // Tracks when a new markdown file is created during `sync`
    21→	EventSyncMarkdownSuccess    = "ext_sync_markdown_success"    // Tracks when a markdown file is updated during `sync`
    22→	EventSyncMarkdownError      = "ext_sync_markdown_error"      // Tracks when an error occurs generating or writing markdown during `sync`
    23→	EventLoginAttempted         = "ext_login_attempted"          // Tracks when user starts the login flow
    24→	EventLoginCancelled         = "ext_login_cancelled"          // Tracks when user cancels the login flow
    25→	EventLoginSuccess           = "ext_login_success"            // Tracks successful login to SpecStory Cloud

    31→// Properties is a type alias for event properties to avoid exposing PostHog types
    32→type Properties map[string]interface{}
    33→
    34→// TrackEvent sends a generic event to PostHog
    35→func TrackEvent(eventName string, properties Properties) {
    36→	if !IsEnabled() {
    37→		return
    38→	}
    39→
    40→	distinctID := GetDistinctID()
    41→
    42→	// Convert to PostHog properties
    43→	phProperties := make(posthog.Properties)
    44→	for k, v := range properties {
    45→		phProperties[k] = v
    46→	}
    47→
    48→	// Always include CLI command, device ID, and project path
    49→	phProperties["cli_command"] = GetCLICommand()
    50→	phProperties["$device_id"] = distinctID
    51→
    52→	// Capture current working directory as project_path
    53→	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
    54→		phProperties["project_path"] = cwd
    55→	}
    56→
    57→	// Agent provider information
    58→	phProperties["agent_provider"] = GetAgentProviderName()
    59→
    60→	// Editor information
    61→	phProperties["editor_name"] = "SpecStory CLI"
    62→	phProperties["editor_type"] = "CLI"
    63→	phProperties["extension_version"] = GetCLIVersion()
    64→
    65→	// OS information (gathered once during initialization)
    66→	osArch, osName, osPlatform, osVersion := GetOSInfo()
    67→	phProperties["os_arch"] = osArch
    68→	phProperties["os_name"] = osName
    69→	phProperties["os_platform"] = osPlatform
    70→	phProperties["os_version"] = osVersion
    71→
    72→	err := client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{
    73→		DistinctId:       distinctID,
    74→		Event:            eventName,
    75→		Properties:       phProperties,
    76→		SendFeatureFlags: false,
    77→	})
    78→

    81→		return
    82→	}

    36→// slogAdapter adapts PostHog's logger interface to use slog at DEBUG level
    37→// This prevents PostHog from writing directly to stderr
    38→type slogAdapter struct{}
    39→
    40→// Logf implements PostHog's Logger interface for info-level messages
    41→// All PostHog log messages are routed to slog.Debug to keep them internal
    42→func (s *slogAdapter) Logf(format string, args ...interface{}) {
    43→	slog.Debug("posthog: "+format, args...)
    44→}
    45→
    46→// Errorf implements PostHog's Logger interface for error-level messages
    47→// Even errors from PostHog (like API failures) are logged at DEBUG level
    48→// since they represent analytics infrastructure issues, not application errors
    49→func (s *slogAdapter) Errorf(format string, args ...interface{}) {
    50→	slog.Debug("posthog error: "+format, args...)
    51→}
    52→
    53→// Debugf implements PostHog's Logger interface for debug-level messages
    54→func (s *slogAdapter) Debugf(format string, args ...interface{}) {
    55→	slog.Debug("posthog debug: "+format, args...)
    56→}
    57→
    58→// Warnf implements PostHog's Logger interface for warning-level messages
    59→func (s *slogAdapter) Warnf(format string, args ...interface{}) {
    60→	slog.Debug("posthog warning: "+format, args...)
    61→}

   117→// generateFallbackID generates a fallback ID from hostname and username
   118→func generateFallbackID() string {

   120→	hostname, _ := os.Hostname()

   142→
   143→// getOSName returns the descriptive OS name from uname (called once during init)
   144→func getOSName() string {
   145→	// Use uname -s for Unix-like systems (Linux, macOS)
   146→	cmd := exec.Command("uname", "-s")
   147→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   148→	if err != nil {
   149→		// Fallback to capitalized GOOS
   150→		return strings.ToUpper(runtime.GOOS[:1]) + runtime.GOOS[1:]
   151→	}
   152→	return strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   153→}
   154→
   155→// getOSVersion returns the OS version (called once during init)
   156→func getOSVersion() string {
   157→	switch runtime.GOOS {
   158→	case "darwin":
   159→		return getMacOSVersion()
   160→	case "linux":
   161→		return getLinuxVersion()
   162→	default:
   163→		return "unknown"
   164→	}
   165→}
   166→
   167→// getMacOSVersion gets the Darwin kernel version using uname to match up with our other extensions os_version property
   168→func getMacOSVersion() string {
   169→	cmd := exec.Command("uname", "-r")
   170→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   171→	if err != nil {
   172→		return "unknown"
   173→	}
   174→	return strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   175→}
   176→
   177→// getLinuxVersion gets the Linux version from various sources
   178→func getLinuxVersion() string {
   179→	// Try /etc/os-release first
   180→	if data, err := os.ReadFile("/etc/os-release"); err == nil {
   181→		lines := strings.Split(string(data), "\n")
   182→		for _, line := range lines {
   183→			if strings.HasPrefix(line, "VERSION_ID=") {
   184→				version := strings.Trim(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "VERSION_ID="), `"`)
   185→				return version
   186→			}
   187→		}
   188→	}
   189→
   190→	// Fallback to uname command
   191→	cmd := exec.Command("uname", "-r")
   192→	if output, err := cmd.Output(); err == nil {
   193→		return strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
   194→	}
   195→
   196→	return "unknown"
   197→}

````markdown
# PostHog Analytics

This document describes the analytics implementation in SpecStory CLI.

## Overview

SpecStory CLI uses PostHog for anonymous usage analytics. Analytics help us understand how the tool is used and improve the product. All tracking is optional and can be disabled.

## Opting Out

To disable analytics, use the `--no-usage-analytics` flag:

```zsh
specstory run --no-usage-analytics
specstory watch --no-usage-analytics
specstory sync --no-usage-analytics
```

## Events Tracked

| Event Key                    | Command   | Description                                           |
|------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------|
| `ext_activated`              | `run`     | Triggered when interactive mode starts                |
| `ext_watch_activated`        | `watch`   | Triggered when watch mode starts                      |
| `ext_autosave_new`           | `run`     | New markdown file created during autosave             |
| `ext_autosave_success`       | `run`     | Markdown file updated during autosave                 |
| `ext_autosave_error`         | `run`     | Error writing markdown during autosave                |
| `ext_sync_markdown_new`      | `sync`    | New markdown file created during sync                 |
| `ext_sync_markdown_success`  | `sync`    | Markdown file updated during sync                     |
| `ext_sync_markdown_error`    | `sync`    | Error writing markdown during sync                    |
| `ext_cloudsync_complete`     | all       | Cloud sync completed with statistics                  |
| `ext_login_attempted`        | `login`   | User started the login flow                           |
| `ext_login_cancelled`        | `login`   | User cancelled the login flow                         |
| `ext_login_success`          | `login`   | Successful login to SpecStory Cloud                   |
| `ext_login_failed`           | `login`   | Failed login attempt                                  |
| `ext_logout`                 | `logout`  | User logged out from SpecStory Cloud                  |
| `ext_project_identity_created` | all     | New project identity created                          |
| `ext_check_install_success`  | `check`   | Successful agent installation check                   |
| `ext_check_install_failed`   | `check`   | Failed agent installation check                       |
| `ext_version_command`        | `version` | User checked the CLI version                          |
| `ext_help_command`           | `help`    | User viewed help                                      |

## Common Properties

Every event automatically includes these properties:

| Property            | Description                                          |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `cli_command`       | Full command line used                               |
| `$device_id`        | Shared analytics ID (see below)                      |
| `project_path`      | Current working directory                            |
| `agent_provider`    | Array of agent provider names (e.g., ["Claude Code"])|
| `editor_name`       | Always "SpecStory CLI"                               |
| `editor_type`       | Always "CLI"                                         |
| `extension_version` | CLI version                                          |
| `os_arch`           | System architecture (e.g., arm64)                    |
| `os_name`           | OS name from uname (e.g., Darwin)                    |
| `os_platform`       | OS platform (e.g., darwin)                           |
| `os_version`        | OS version                                           |

## Shared Analytics ID

On macOS, SpecStory CLI shares an analytics ID with other SpecStory applications (like BearClaude) to provide a unified view of usage across tools.

**Location:** `~/Library/Application Support/SpecStory/analytics-id.json`

**Format:**

```json
{
  "analytics_id": "uuid-here",
  "created_at": "2025-01-20T10:00:00Z",
  "source": "specstory-cli"
}
```

On non-macOS systems or if the shared ID cannot be read, a fallback ID is generated from a hash of the hostname and username.

## Configuration

The PostHog API key is injected at build time via ldflags. Development builds have analytics disabled (empty API key).

See `.goreleaser.yml` for build configuration and `.github/workflows/release.yml` for how the `POSTHOG_API_KEY` secret is passed during release builds.

## Implementation

The analytics code is in `pkg/analytics/`:

- `client.go` - PostHog client initialization and configuration
- `events.go` - Event constants and the `TrackEvent` function
- `shared_id.go` - Shared analytics ID management

````

    56→	}

    60→

    62→	phProperties["editor_name"] = "SpecStory CLI"
    63→	phProperties["editor_type"] = "CLI"
    64→	phProperties["extension_version"] = GetCLIVersion()
    65→
    66→	// OS information (gathered once during initialization)
    67→	osArch, osName, osPlatform, osVersion := GetOSInfo()
    68→	phProperties["os_arch"] = osArch
    69→	phProperties["os_name"] = osName
    70→	phProperties["os_platform"] = osPlatform
    71→	phProperties["os_version"] = osVersion
    72→
    73→	err := client.Enqueue(posthog.Capture{

    75→		Event:            eventName,
    76→		Properties:       phProperties,

    79→

```text
     1→# PostHog Analytics
     2→
     3→This document describes the analytics implementation in SpecStory CLI.
     4→
     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→SpecStory CLI uses PostHog for anonymous usage analytics. Analytics help us understand how the tool is used and improve the product. All tracking is optional and can be disabled.
     8→
     9→## Opting Out
    10→
    11→To disable analytics, use the `--no-usage-analytics` flag:
    12→
    13→```zsh
    14→specstory run --no-usage-analytics
    15→specstory watch --no-usage-analytics
    16→specstory sync --no-usage-analytics
    17→```
    18→
    19→## Events Tracked
    20→
    21→| Event Key                    | Command   | Description                                           |
    22→|------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------|
    23→| `ext_activated`              | `run`     | Triggered when interactive mode starts                |
    24→| `ext_watch_activated`        | `watch`   | Triggered when watch mode starts                      |
    25→| `ext_autosave_new`           | `run`     | New markdown file created during autosave             |
    26→| `ext_autosave_success`       | `run`     | Markdown file updated during autosave                 |
    27→| `ext_autosave_error`         | `run`     | Error writing markdown during autosave                |
    28→| `ext_sync_markdown_new`      | `sync`    | New markdown file created during sync                 |
    29→| `ext_sync_markdown_success`  | `sync`    | Markdown file updated during sync                     |
    30→| `ext_sync_markdown_error`    | `sync`    | Error writing markdown during sync                    |
    31→| `ext_cloudsync_complete`     | all       | Cloud sync completed with statistics                  |
    32→| `ext_login_attempted`        | `login`   | User started the login flow                           |
    33→| `ext_login_cancelled`        | `login`   | User cancelled the login flow                         |
    34→| `ext_login_success`          | `login`   | Successful login to SpecStory Cloud                   |
    35→| `ext_login_failed`           | `login`   | Failed login attempt                                  |
    36→| `ext_logout`                 | `logout`  | User logged out from SpecStory Cloud                  |
    37→| `ext_project_identity_created` | all     | New project identity created                          |
    38→| `ext_check_install_success`  | `check`   | Successful agent installation check                   |
    39→| `ext_check_install_failed`   | `check`   | Failed agent installation check                       |
    40→| `ext_version_command`        | `version` | User checked the CLI version                          |
    41→| `ext_help_command`           | `help`    | User viewed help                                      |
    42→
    43→## Common Properties
    44→
    45→Every event automatically includes these properties:
    46→
    47→| Property            | Description                                          |
    48→|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
    49→| `cli_command`       | Full command line used                               |
    50→| `$device_id`        | Shared analytics ID (see below)                      |
    51→| `project_path`      | Current working directory                            |
    52→| `agent_provider`    | Array of agent provider names (e.g., ["Claude Code"])|
    53→| `editor_name`       | Always "SpecStory CLI"                               |
    54→| `editor_type`       | Always "CLI"                                         |
    55→| `extension_version` | CLI version                                          |
    56→| `os_arch`           | System architecture (e.g., arm64)                    |
    57→| `os_name`           | OS name from uname (e.g., Darwin)                    |
    58→| `os_platform`       | OS platform (e.g., darwin)                           |
    59→| `os_version`        | OS version                                           |
    60→
    61→## Shared Analytics ID
    62→
    63→On macOS, SpecStory CLI shares an analytics ID with other SpecStory applications (like BearClaude) to provide a unified view of usage across tools.
    64→
    65→**Location:** `~/Library/Application Support/SpecStory/analytics-id.json`
    66→
    67→**Format:**
    68→
    69→```json
    70→{
    71→  "analytics_id": "uuid-here",
    72→  "created_at": "2025-01-20T10:00:00Z",
    73→  "source": "specstory-cli"
    74→}
    75→```
    76→
    77→On non-macOS systems or if the shared ID cannot be read, a fallback ID is generated from a hash of the hostname and username.
    78→
    79→## Configuration
    80→
    81→The PostHog API key is injected at build time via ldflags. Development builds have analytics disabled (empty API key).
    82→
    83→See `.goreleaser.yml` for build configuration and `.github/workflows/release.yml` for how the `POSTHOG_API_KEY` secret is passed during release builds.
    84→
    85→## Implementation
    86→
    87→The analytics code is in `pkg/analytics/`:
    88→
    89→- `client.go` - PostHog client initialization and configuration
    90→- `events.go` - Event constants and the `TrackEvent` function
    91→- `shared_id.go` - Shared analytics ID management
    92→
```
</details></tool-use>
